title: Dresden Day Trip from Prague
short_description: Spend a day in Dresden with your own Mercedes and chauffeur. Door to door from your Prague address, one price for the whole car, and time in the old town built into your booking.
description:
Dresden is the capital of Saxony, a baroque city on the Elbe that was rebuilt stone by stone after 1945. It lies just across the border from Prague, and its old town is compact, so one day is enough to see the best of it without hurrying.

Your chauffeur collects you at your address in Prague at the time you choose and drives you north, over the border and down the Elbe valley. You are dropped at the edge of the old town. From there the Frauenkirche, the Procession of Princes, the Zwinger and the Semper Opera are all within a short walk of each other.

The car and the chauffeur then wait for you for the time included in your booking, which is shown next to the price. You decide how to spend it: the old town on foot, the Old Masters Picture Gallery, a walk along the Brühl Terrace, a long lunch. If you want more time, add extra hours when you book. Time beyond that on the day is charged only after a person at Prestigo agrees to it.

The price is for the whole car, not per person. It covers the drive there and back, fuel, motorway tolls and your time in Dresden. You see the total before you pay, and the same car and chauffeur bring you back to the door where the day began.

Your chauffeur is a professional driver, not a guide. Entrance tickets, guided tours and meals are not included. If you would like a licensed local guide, book one for the hours you plan to be there and we will help you time the day around it.
highlights: The Frauenkirche, rebuilt and reconsecrated in 2005, a few minutes from where you are dropped
The Zwinger palace and the Semper Opera on the same square
The Procession of Princes, a long wall of porcelain tiles in the old town
The Brühl Terrace above the Elbe, for the view and a coffee
Time for one museum, such as the Old Masters Picture Gallery with Raphael’s Sistine Madonna
A second country in one day, without changing trains

itinerary.title: Pickup at your Prague address
itinerary.body: Your chauffeur meets you at the door of your hotel or apartment in Prague at the time you chose. If you asked for child seats, they are already fitted.

itinerary.title: Drive north to Saxony
itinerary.body: The route runs on the motorway through northern Bohemia, over the border and down into the Elbe valley. Both countries are in the Schengen area, so the border is normally just a sign by the road.

itinerary.title: Arrival at the old town
itinerary.body: Your chauffeur drops you at the edge of the old town and tells you where the car will wait. From here almost everything is on foot.

itinerary.title: The old town on foot
itinerary.body: Walk to the Frauenkirche, along the Procession of Princes, through the Zwinger courtyard and past the Semper Opera. The Brühl Terrace is a short walk from the church.

itinerary.title: A museum, a market or a long lunch
itinerary.body: Use the rest of your time as you like. In December the Striezelmarkt, one of the oldest Christmas markets in Germany, fills the old town. Call or message your chauffeur when you are ready.

itinerary.title: The drive back
itinerary.body: The chauffeur collects you where you were dropped off and drives back up the Elbe valley and over the border. Rest, read or sleep in the back.

itinerary.title: Return to your Prague address
itinerary.body: The same car and chauffeur bring you back to the same address in Prague where the day began.

includes: A private Mercedes with your own chauffeur, for your party only
Pickup and return at your address in Prague
The drive to Dresden and back
Waiting time at the destination for the hours included in your booking
Child seats at no charge: tell us the children’s ages when you book
One price for the whole car, shown in full before you pay
excludes: Entrance tickets, for example to the museums or the Green Vault
A guide or a guided tour: your chauffeur drives and waits, but is not a guide
Extra hours beyond your booking, unless you add them when you book
pickup_info: Pickup and return are at your address in Prague: a hotel, an apartment or an office. Tell us the exact address when you book. Before the day you receive your chauffeur’s name and phone number, and on the day they wait at the door at the agreed time.
important_info:
Carry a passport or national ID. Both countries are in the Schengen area and there is normally no check at the border, but police may ask for documents, and visitors from outside the EU need a valid passport and, where required, a Schengen visa.

Many Dresden museums are closed on Mondays, and the Old Masters Picture Gallery is among them. Check the day before you fix the date.

The Historic Green Vault admits visitors by timed ticket. Book it before you travel.

Germany uses the euro and the Czech Republic the koruna. Cards are accepted in most places in Dresden, but smaller cafés and market stalls often prefer cash.

Your chauffeur drives and waits, but is not a guide. Entrance tickets and guided tours are not included.

faq.q: How is the price worked out?
faq.a: There is one price for the whole car, set for each car class. It covers the drive there and back, fuel, motorway tolls and the hours at the destination included in your booking. You can add extra hours when you book, and you see the total before you pay.

faq.q: Does the chauffeur wait and drive us back the same day?
faq.a: Yes. The same car and chauffeur take you to Dresden, wait for the time you booked and drive you back to your Prague address. Waiting during the hours in your booking is part of the price.

faq.q: What if we want to stay longer on the day?
faq.a: Tell your chauffeur. Time beyond your booking is charged only after a person at Prestigo agrees to it, at the same extra-hour price you saw when you booked. Nothing is charged automatically.

faq.q: Is a guide or an entrance ticket included?
faq.a: No. The price covers the car and the chauffeur. Tickets and guided tours are booked separately, and the chauffeur does not act as a guide. We are glad to help you time the day around a guide or a ticket slot you have booked.

faq.q: Do we need passports for a day trip to Dresden?
faq.a: Yes, carry a passport or national ID. Both countries are in the Schengen area and there is normally no check at the border, but police may ask for documents.

faq.q: How many people fit in one car?
faq.a: Up to three passengers in an E-Class or S-Class and up to six in a V-Class. Larger groups travel in two or more cars. Child seats are free in every class.
